original_question: Can one determine a single model together with an adequate optimization technique that simultaneously accounts for many different characteristics of computer-network operation quality?
target_in_paper: The draft points to the second unnumbered open problem in Section C, "Open Problems Related to Computer Networks," which asks for one unified model for multiple characteristics of network-operation quality together with a technique to optimize them. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper's target problem: it asks for a single model, it asks for an optimization technique, and it understands that the model is meant to handle multiple characteristics of the quality of computer-network operation at once. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
missing_details: The draft omits the paper's explicit setting: the topological design of complex computer networks with optimum performance, not an abstract optimization problem detached from network topology. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

It omits the graph-theoretic context that motivates the question: the paper says certain classes of graphs, specifically geodetic graphs, are better suited for obtaining optimal indices of network-operation quality. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

It does not name the quality characteristics listed by the paper, namely systemic hierarchy, diameter, vertex connectivity, reliability, cost, and flexibility of topological change, among others. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

It does not distinguish this problem from the neighboring but different open problem on the same page: studying how changes in connection topology influence network-performance quality. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

The paper gives no formal variables, objective function, constraint set, admissible family of graphs, or optimization paradigm (for example, weighted, lexicographic, or Pareto); a stand-alone reformulation should therefore stay qualitative and not pretend that the paper specifies a formal theorem-level model. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))

No ambient ring, field, operator notation, homogeneity, degree restriction, nilpotency condition, or asymptotic quantifier is part of the target statement here, because the relevant item is an unnumbered graph/network-design open problem rather than an algebraic conjecture. ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
refined_question: In the topological design of complex computer networks, and in the geodetic-graph setting emphasized in the paper, can one determine a single unified model that simultaneously takes into account multiple characteristics of the quality of network operation—such as systemic hierarchy, diameter, vertex connectivity, reliability, cost, and flexibility of topological change—and also determine an adequate technique for optimizing those characteristics within that one model? ([dizzw.com](https://dizzw.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Deutsche-internationale-Zeitschrift-f%C3%BCr-zeitgen%C3%B6ssische-Wissenschaft-%E2%84%9636-2022.pdf))
justification: This is the closest paper-faithful target because the wording of your draft matches the second open problem in Section C almost directly, whereas Sections A and B concern characterization, construction, and enumeration of geodetic graphs, and Section D concerns computer-science connections through rewriting systems. The paper does not contain items labeled Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3, so the relevant target is this unnumbered open problem instead. The refinement adds only context explicitly supplied nearby in the paper: the network-design setting, the listed quality indices, and the surrounding geodetic-graph motivation; it deliberately does not merge in the separate question about how topology changes affect performance. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.10663))
